Upward: senior management, sponsor. Downward: the team. Outward: suppliers, regulators, end users. Sideward: peers of the project manager.
The component of the project management plan with the strategies and actions for promoting productive involvement of stakeholders.
Compares each stakeholder's current (C) and desired (D) engagement level. The gap shows where effort is needed.
Unaware, resistant, neutral, supportive, leading.
Supportive: aware and in favor of the work and its outcomes. Leading: aware and actively engaged in making the project a success.
Describes how, when and by whom project information will be administered and disseminated, including the escalation process.
Determines the information needs of the project stakeholders, combining the type and format of information with its value.
n(n − 1) ÷ 2, where n is the number of people. Count the project manager.
A real-time, multidirectional exchange between two or more parties: meetings, phone calls, videoconferences, instant messaging.
Sent to specific recipients: emails, memos, reports, letters. Ensures distribution, not that it was received or understood.
Recipients access the content themselves when they choose: web portals, intranet sites, knowledge repositories. For large audiences or large amounts of information.
Encode, transmit, decode, acknowledge, feedback/response.
Anything that interferes with the understanding of a message: distance, technology, distraction, language, culture.
A clear and complete message, and confirming that it was correctly understood.
Receiving the whole message, interpreting it correctly, and acknowledging or responding.

front: Does acknowledging a message mean agreeing with it?
back: No. Acknowledgment only signals that the message was received.
Communicating and working with stakeholders to meet needs, address issues and foster involvement. Benefit: increases support and minimizes resistance.
Timely and appropriate collection, creation, distribution, storage, retrieval and final disposition of project information. Output: project communications.
Urgency, availability and reliability of the technology, ease of use, project environment, and sensitivity and confidentiality of the information.
Initiates the project, approves the charter and the plan, assigns and empowers the project manager, secures resources, authorizes completion.
